**1 — Scene:** A cheeseburger with a separate slice of toasted white bread.

**2 — Vessel:** A large dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across. Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Burger bun, beef patty, melted cheese, a little lettuce/pickle and pale sauce; one slice of toast. I’ll calculate the stacked burger as one item to avoid double-counting its footprint. No separate butter or oil is clearly visible.

**4 — Area:** Burger approximately **22%** of the plate (117 cm²); toast approximately **20%** (106 cm²). Total coverage: **42%**, consistent with the substantial empty plate.

**5–7 — Volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Area × average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cheeseburger, including visible toppings | 117 × 5.5 cm | 644 ml | 0.40 g/ml | 258 g | 255 | 658 kcal |
| White toast | 106 × 1.3 cm | 138 ml | 0.30 g/ml | 41 g | 280 | 115 kcal |

The burger’s composite density accounts for its airy bun and denser filling. Toast uses porous loaf-bread density. Neither receives any additional air/gap reduction.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **300 g and 770 kcal** is plausible for the visible burger and thick toast slice. The main uncertainties are the patty thickness and amount of sauce.
